title: API robustness: standardize Retry-After, idempotency and error codes for streaming + OpenAI-compat
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: We have recurring customer issues and flaky behavior when streaming responses combined with transient rate-limits and retries. Different endpoints returned inconsistent Retry-After semantics and non-uniform error codes (sometimes 429 with no header, sometimes 503, occasionally 500). This caused client-side retry logic and idempotency handling to be brittle, and broke OpenAI-compatibility expectations for SDKs.
Motivation: Standardize server behavior so clients can reliably back off, replay idempotent requests, and recover streaming sessions when appropriate. This PR converges behavior across the text generation, chat streaming, and function-calling codepaths and aligns with OpenAI-compat patterns.
Summary of changes:
- Add uniform Retry-After header and a deterministic Retry-After body field for JSON responses when rate-limited; Retry-After is emitted for 429 and 503 where applicable.
- Enforce idempotency-key behavior: idempotency keys are checked early for streaming and non-streaming requests; conflicting replay attempts return 409 with a clear body ("idempotency_conflict": true) and guidance.
- Streaming reconnect guidance: when a streaming connection is terminated due to transient rate-limit, the server emits an event with a controlled close reason and the Retry-After; SDKs can use this to wait and resume with the same idempotency key where model supports resumed generation.
- Consistent error codes: map transient service overload to 503 + Retry-After, hit quota to 429 + Retry-After, auth failures to 401, invalid input to 400.
- OpenAI-compat layer: ensure compatibility headers and bodies for clients expecting OpenAI semantics (uses camelCase fields and top-level "error" object when applicable).
- Tests and docs: expand integration tests for streaming reconnect scenarios, add unit tests for idempotency key collisions, update API spec and SDK compatibility doc.
Implementation notes:
- Server-side changes span api-gateway (retry-after propagation), runtime request router (idempotency key short-circuit), and streaming transport layer (graceful close event + structured close payload).
- New middleware: idempotency middleware that stores in the existing fast cache with explicit short TTLs for streaming in-flight requests.
- Backwards compatible: default behavior is unchanged for clients that do not read Retry-After or idempotency headers; header names and body fields are additive.
- Rollout plan: feature-flagged; Gradual rollout to 10% of traffic for 24h, then 50% then 100% after metrics look good.
Monitoring: we added dashboards for idempotency_conflict_rate, retry_after_emitted_count, streaming_reconnects, and the rate-limit SLO alert.
Testing: added deterministic unit tests and end-to-end tests that simulate quota spikes, network interruption on streaming, and idempotency replay.
Checklist:
- [x] Idempotency middleware implemented and unit tested
- [x] Retry-After header/body standardized and tested
- [x] Streaming transport emits structured close payload
- [x] OpenAI-compat response shapes validated
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Docs updated in redwood-docs and SDKs
- [x] Feature flag & rollout plan added
Related: ENG-4821 (idempotency improvements), ENG-4905 (streaming stability), SUP-1127 (customer incident repro).

release_notes: Standardized Retry-After semantics and idempotency behavior across streaming and non-streaming endpoints; added structured streaming close payload to aid SDK resume logic; improved OpenAI-compat error shapes.
notes_for_ops: Feature-flag controlled; rollout plan attached in PR description. Watch idempotency_conflict_rate and streaming_reconnects dashboards. If regressions occur, toggle feature flag to rollback per-service.
